To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
anatoxin a, a nicotinic agonists, releases dopamine from rat striatal nerve terminals by activating voltage-dependent Ca2+ channels.
activation of nicotinic receptors on nerve terminals by anatoxin a results in an influx, of Na(+) that opens Ca2+ channels and triggers exocytosis.

the nicotinic agonists anatoxin-a, nicotine and acetylcholine, when applied to striatal nerve terminals, stimulate [3H]DA release by a process that is dependent upon Ca2+ entry through voltage-sensitive Ca2+-channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms coupling nicotic receptor activation to exocyctosis.
the mechanisms of nicotinic receptor-mediated neurotransmitter release, with a view to developing new drugs to treat neurological and psychiatric disorders.
the mechanisms of exocytosis in the central nervous system, and in particular the role of presynaptic cholinergic nicotinic receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
anatoxin-evoked [3h]dopamine exocytosis from striatal synaptosome is mediated by Ca(2+) influx through voltage-sensitive Ca(2+) and Na(+) channels.

the mechanism of anatoxin-evoked dopamine release from the striatum is a combination of direct and indirect effects, the direct effect being a consequence of the opening of voltage-gated Ca2+ channels.
anatoxin a, a selective nicotinic acetycholine receptor agonist, stimulates the release of [3H]DA from rat striatal nerve endings by activating voltage-sensitive Ca2+, and possibly Na+, channels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presynaptic nicotiinic receptor on the nerve terminals of the striatal dopaminergic neurons is coupled to the release of dopamine by an influx of Ca2+.
anatoxin-evoked release from striatal synaptosomal preparations is a Ca2(+)-dependent process that involves both Na+ and Ca2+ channels.
anatoxin is a potent and selective nicotinic acetycholine agonist that stimulates dopamine release from rat striatum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
anatoxin is a useful tool to explore nicotinic receptor-mediated exocytosis.
the presynaptic modulation of neurotransmitter release by nicotinic receptor stimulation is not limited to the central cholinergic synapses.
anatoxin a is an effective agonist at nicotinic acetycholine receptors on presynaptic terminals of dopaminergic neurons.
